target_customer: Independent gas station owners and truck stop operators in the United States
problem: Independent retailers faced card network chip (EMV) and fraud requirements at the pump that cost tens of thousands of dollars per pump to meet, and fuel card fees at truck stops were high.
business_model: SaaS and hardware retrofit with no upfront cost and a small monthly fee (about $200 per month plus 2% of card transactions for the truck stop product, per 2019 press)
product_category: fintech infrastructure / fuel point of sale and pump payment upgrades

founders.name: Joshua Smith
founders.background_notes: Described as 34 and CEO in the Nov 2018 Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette article; no employer or education details found.

founders.name: Nannette Smith
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio found.

competitors.name: Comdata (FleetCor)
competitors.what: fuel card network whose fees the truck stop product aimed to undercut

competitors.name: EFS (WEX)
competitors.what: fuel card network whose fees the truck stop product aimed to undercut

competitors.name: Gilbarco Veeder-Root
competitors.what: pump maker selling in-pump chip (EMV) hardware to retailers
competitors.traction_then: said more than half of the top 200 oil retailers had installed in-pump chip hardware

competitors.name: Verifone
competitors.what: payment terminal vendor working with dispenser makers on chip requirements

technical_complexity.rationale: A plug-in retrofit module for existing pumps plus payment integrations requires hardware certification and card network compliance, which is moderately hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Certification and installed hardware create switching costs, and long-time pump providers reportedly expected a new entrant to need three years to build a competing solution.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pump makers and payment vendors sold their own chip upgrades and the card networks extended deadlines; no acquisition of Gas Pos was found.

market_need_then: Card networks required chip acceptance at the pump with an October 2020 liability shift date (later extended per some sources); independents faced estimates of $80,000 to $160,000 to upgrade, and the CEO called skimming out of control.

branding.domain_note: Uses gaspos.co (a .co domain); the .com history was not found.

branding.brand_signature: Truck stop product named Steve, a virtual payment network

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that reads as generic and is hard to search; no press about the brand or community found.

outcome_analysis: Gas Pos began in Birmingham, graduated from a 2018 FIS accelerator, raised $1M from Merus Capital in 2018 and joined YC in Winter 2020 with a card-network driven pump upgrade and a truck stop payments product. The company is listed as active, but no later rounds, growth data or exit were found, so the outcome is unclear.
notes: Company website gaspos.co returned 404 on fetch (possibly dead). Round stage is other because the article does not state a label; round date is the article date. Unverified figures: FundedIQ shows $200k across one undisclosed round in 2020-03, CB Insights shows $1.7M total, geo.sig.ai shows $1.15M to $3.73M and a Mexico City location that conflicts with every other source. HQ moved from Birmingham, Alabama to North Little Rock, Arkansas in 2018 with a pledge of 30 jobs.
